questions.question:
**Direction: Select the grammatically correct version of the following sentence.**

I like my puppies, Mac and Matt, but I like Matt best.

options.text: I like my puppies, Mac and Matt, but I like Matt better.
I like my puppies, Mac and Matt, but I like Matt the best.
I like my puppies, Mac and Matt, but I like Matt much.
I like my puppies, Mac and Matt, but I like Matt most.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"I like my puppies, Mac and Matt, but I like Matt better."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In this context, the error lies in the word **"best."**
 
• The word "best" is the superlative form of "good," which is used when comparing three or more things.
 
 
• **Example**: *She is the **best**__ of all.*
 
 
 
• The word** "better"** is the comparative form of the adjective** "good,"** which is the correct form to use when comparing two things.
 __
 
• **Example**: *Karan is **better**__ than Arun.*
 
 
 
• In this sentence, we are comparing two puppies, so the correct answer is Option 1.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2: "best"** is the superlative form of "good," but it is used incorrectly in this context because the sentence only compares two things.
 
• **Option 3: "much"** is an adverb that describes the degree or extent of something, but it is not appropriate in this context.
 
• **Option 4: "most"** is a superlative form, but it is not used correctly in this context.

questions.question:
**Direction: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.**

Do the Basus visit the Shuklas?

options.text: Are the Shuklas been visited by the Basus?
Are the Shuklas visit by the Basus?
Are the Shuklas being visited by the Basus?
Are the Shuklas visited by the Basus?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Are the Shuklas visited by the Basus? **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

 
• The given sentence is in active voice, where the subject **"Basus"** is performing the action of visiting.
 
• To convert it into passive voice, we need to make the object** "Shuklas"** the subject and add a form of **"be"** before the past participle **"visited".**
 
• The resulting sentence will have the object **"Basus" **after** "by",** indicating who performed the action.
 
• Also, the verb is placed before the subject in the Passive Voice.
 
• **Structure:**
 
• *Do/does + Subject + V1 + Object?* (Active Voice)
 
• *Is/am/are + Object + V2 + by + Subject?* (Passive Voice)
 
• **Example**:
 
 
• *Does Rahul love his parents?* (Active)
 
• *Are the parents loved by Rahul*? (Passive)
 
 
 
• The correct answer is Option 4.

Therefore, the correct answer is: ***Are the Shuklas visited by the Basus? ***

A) about all his

B) noise they make

questions.solution:

__
 
• The sentence should start with the subject, which is **"he"** in this case.
 
• So, the first part is **C**.
 
• The next part should be the **verb + preposition**, which is **"complains about all his."**
 
• So, the next part is** A.**
 
• Then, we need to add the object, which is **"about all his neighbours and the noise they make."**
 
• So, the next pair must be **DB**.
 
• The correct answer is option 2.

 

**Correct sentence**:* H**e constantly complains about all his neighbours and the noise they make.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1 (B, A, D, C) **is incorrect because it starts with the object instead of the subject.

I was kept waiting for more than an hour to get an appointment by the staff.

The staff kept me waiting for more than an hour to get an appointment.

• The given sentence is in Passive Voice. It is in Simple Past Tense. As per the given question we have to change it into Active Voice. 
 
• The structure of Simple Past Tense is as follows:
 
 
• Subject + V2 + Object. (Active Voice)
 
• Subject (objective case)+ was/were + V3 + Object (subjective case). (Passive Voice)
 
 
 
• Example:
 
 
• *Their cousin showed them some rare photographs. (Active Voice)*
 
• *They were shown some rare photographs by their cousin. (Passive Voice)*
 
 
 
• In the passive voice, the subject is** "I"** and the object is **"staff."**
 
• So, in the active voice, the subject would be** "staff" **and the object would be** "me." **
 
 
• 'Was kept' will be changed into 'kept.'
 
 
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.
